articles.title: Newscast - Can Milburn's Neets Report Help Britain's 'Lost Generation'? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Alan Milburn wants to get more young people earning or learning but can his reforms work?
articles.body: Today, Alan Milburn's long awaited report into young people not in education, employment, or training - "Neet" - has been published. Nearly one million young people in the UK are not earning or learning. In his report, Milburn sets out an extensive set of reforms to try and reach a target he calls Neet Zero… or reducing the number of young Neets down from 15% to 5% by 2036. Adam and Chris Mason are joined by education and family editor, Branwen Jeffreys, to unpack the 267-page report and assess how feasible its recommendations are. articles.title: What in the World - How does vaping affect your singing voice? - BBC Sounds
articles.summary: Selena Gomez is the latest celebrity to speak about it
articles.body:
World Service , · 17 Nov 2026 , · 8 mins

“It’s so stupid and it changed my voice”- that’s what Selena Gomez recently said about vaping nicotine. She’s now stopped, but what could the long term affects be for people who use vapes? There aren’t many scientific studies yet with proof about how vaping may impact your health and your vocals. But anecdotally, there are examples of singers who say they are losing vocal range and their tone is being affected after vaping or smoking e-cigarettes. We speak to Cypriot singer and vocal coach Alex Panayi about changes he’s noticed in singers who vape, and Los Angeles-based medical doctor Reena Gupta tells us how it may impact the voice. articles.title: Acre teve 9 pessoas assassinadas em 1 semana em disputa entre facções | G1
articles.standfirst: Do total, sete ocorreram em Rio Branco e dois no interior. Entre as vítimas, algumas foram mortas em suas residências e outras em vias públicas. Parte delas era monitorada por tornozeleira.
articles.summary: Do total, sete ocorreram em Rio Branco e dois no interior. Entre as vítimas, algumas foram mortas em suas residências e arte delas era monitorada por tornozeleira.
articles.body:
Nove pessoas foram assassinadas no Acre em um intervalo de uma semana, entre terça-feira (10) e a noite desta segunda-feira (16), em meio a um cenário de violência relacionado à disputa entre facções criminosas. Do total de vítimas, sete foram mortas em Rio Branco e duas no interior.

Na capital, os crimes ocorreram principalmente no Segundo Distrito, região onde moradores mais sentem insegurança em Rio Branco. Entre as vítimas, que tinham entre 18 e 35 anos, parte dos casos ocorreu dentro de residências.

⏩ A sequência de assassinatos ocorre em meio a investigações sobre conflitos entre facções criminosas que atuam no Acre. Ao g1 , o delegado Alcino Ferreira Júnior informou que os assassinatos podem desencadear uma série de represálias entre grupos rivais.

Contudo, a corporação ainda trabalha para esclarecer a participação dos suspeitos e as motivações dos assassinatos. Segundo ele, a expectativa é que pelo menos parte dos executores seja colocada à disposição da Justiça até o final desta semana.

Cinco vítimas foram mortas a tiros entre terça-feira (10) e quinta-feira (12), em Rio Branco — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

"Cada vez que há um homicídio, há uma represália imediata, então acaba que acontece um combo de mortes. A gente tem trabalhado para identificar não só quem executa esses crimes, mas também quem está por trás das ordens. A expectativa é que até a próxima semana a gente tenha pelo menos esses executores à disposição da Justiça", afirmou.

No recorte de uma semana, o primeiro caso foi de Ruan Vítor Araújo Brasiliano, de 23 anos , morto na madrugada de terça-feira (10), após ter a casa invadida por três homens armados na Travessa Manancial, no bairro Belo Jardim I.

Segundo a Polícia Militar do Acre (PM-AC), os suspeitos usavam roupas semelhantes às de policiais, além de coletes e coturnos. No momento da invasão, Ruan dormia no quarto ao lado da esposa, que presenciou o assassinato.

Ainda na terça, Antônio Carlos dos Santos Jardim , de 31 anos, e Wenisson Nick Ponceano Souza , de 20, foram encontrados mortos em uma área de mata próxima à quadra 22 do Conjunto Habitacional Cidade do Povo, no Segundo Distrito.

Os dois estavam com as mãos amarradas e apresentavam marcas de tiros na cabeça. Os corpos foram localizados por uma equipe da Divisão de Monitoramento Eletrônico (DME) da Polícia Penal, que fazia buscas por uma tornozeleira eletrônica violada e retirada de um dos monitorados.

Dois homens foram encontrados mortos com tiros na cabeça em uma área de mata em Rio Branco — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Também na terça, Rafael da Conceição Miller, de 20 anos , foi morto a tiros enquanto caminhava ao lado da esposa pelo Ramal Santa Fé, no bairro Benfica, região da Vila Acre. Segundo a PM-AC, Rafael era monitorado por tornozeleira eletrônica e foi perseguido por dois homens antes de morrer.

Já na na quinta-feira (12), André Felipe da Silva Rocha, de 18 anos , foi encontrado baleado na cabeça em um terreno na Rua Baguari, no bairro Taquari. Moradores que passavam pelo local encontraram o jovem ferido, mas ele não resistiu aos ferimentos e morreu no hospital.

Além disso, Carlos Daniel do Santos Sarmento, de 19 anos , foi encontrado morto dentro de uma casa na Travessa da Judia, no bairro Recanto dos Buritis, no Segundo Distrito de Rio Branco, no domingo (15). Segundo a PM-AC, ele estava com as mãos amarradas, amordaçado e foi ferido na cabeça.

Por último, nessa segunda-feira (16), Cleberton Cosme de Oliveira Batista, de 35 anos , foi morto a tiros na Rua Boulevard Augusto Monteiro, no Bairro Quinze, no Segundo Distrito de Rio Branco. Ele era monitorado por tornozeleira eletrônica e foi abordada por dois homens em uma motocicleta.

Cleberton Cosme de Oliveira Batista foi morto a tiros na Rua Boulevard Augusto Monteiro, no Bairro Quinze — Foto: Pedro Marcelo/Rede Amazônica Acre

Além dos sete homicídios em Rio Branco, outros dois assassinatos foram contabilizados no interior do Acre durante o mesmo período. Em Capixaba , no interior do Acre, Antônio Brasil Pereira, de 46 anos , foi morto a tiros dentro da própria casa, na terça-feira (10), enquanto estava com a família.

Conforme a Polícia Militar (PM-AC), o crime ocorreu no Ramal da Elza, na Reserva São Luiz do Remanso. De acordo com o boletim de ocorrência, um homem armado chegou de motocicleta, invadiu a residência e efetuou vários disparos contra a vítima.

Antônio Brasil Pereira, de 46 anos, foi morto a tiros dentro de casa, em Capixaba — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Já em Epitaciolândia , também no interior do estado, um adolescente de 17 anos foi morto a tiros na madrugada de sexta-feira (13), na região do bairro Liberdade. Conforme a ocorrência, ele trafegava em uma bicicleta elétrica quando foi perseguido por um suspeito, que teria corrido atrás dele

A sequência de homicídios também remete a um cenário registrado no início de 2017, quando o Acre contabilizou pelo menos 25 mortes violentas nos primeiros 12 dias daquele ano. Os dados da Secretaria de Segurança Pública à época incluíam mortes por armas de fogo e armas brancas.

Na ocasião, o então responsável pela Delegacia de Homicídios e Proteção à Pessoa (DHPP) de Rio Branco, delegado Roberth Alencar, informou que 14 casos registrados na capital eram investigados pela unidade.

Segundo ele, os crimes apresentavam características semelhantes, como mortes por arma de fogo, suspeitos em motocicletas e vítimas abordadas por desconhecidos. O delegado afirmou que as investigações preliminares apontavam para possíveis motivações relacionadas interesses de facções.

articles.title: Forte turbulência em voo para os EUA deixa feridos | G1
articles.standfirst: Equipes de emergência tiveram que ser acionadas quando o avião aterrissou no aeroporto de Fort Lauderdale, na Flórida.
articles.summary: Equipes de emergência tiveram que ser acionadas quando o avião aterrissou no aeroporto de Fort Lauderdale, na Flórida.
articles.body:
Trajeto do voo 1717 da JetBlue que enfrentou forte turbulência entre Porto Rico e a Flórida — Foto: Flight Aware/ Reprodução

Uma forte turbulência deixou vários feridos em um voo da empresa aérea JetBlue, que saiu de Porto Rico com destino a Fort Lauderdale, na Flórida, sul dos Estados Unidos, nesta terça-feira (17).

Segundo o Corpo de Bombeiros, cinco pessoas tiveram ferimentos ou precisaram de atendimento médico quando o avião aterrissou no aeroporto, por volta das 7h do horário local (9h no horário de Brasília). Nenhuma delas, no entanto, precisou ser levada para o hospital.

"A aeronave pousou em segurança por volta das 6h58 e seguiu para o Terminal 3, onde a equipe do Corpo de Bombeiros do Condado de Broward estava de prontidão para avaliar as pessoas que relataram ferimentos. Os bombeiros identificaram cinco indivíduos que relataram ferimentos ou que necessitavam de avaliação", informou a unidade.

As autoridades também confirmaram que não houve relatos de danos estruturais à aeronave.

Em um comunicado oficial à imprensa, a JetBlue confirmou o incidente com o voo 1717 e afirmou:

"A segurança de nossos clientes e tripulantes continua sendo nossa principal prioridade".

Imagem de junho de 2013 mostra aviões da Jetblue no aeroporto de Nova York, EUA — Foto: REUTERS/Fred Prouser

articles.title: STF inaugura símbolo de Xangô, orixá da Justiça, no edifício-sede | G1
articles.standfirst: Escultura do Oxê de Xangô será instalada no edifício-sede do Supremo, em Brasília. Pedido foi feito após decisão da Corte que permitiu símbolos religiosos em prédios públicos.
articles.summary: A escultura Oxê de Xangô foi instalada no STF após decisão sobre símbolos religiosos em prédios públicos, representando um marco para as religiões de matriz africana.
articles.body:
Oxê de Xangô, símbolo da Justiça na tradição iorubá e das religiões de matriz africana — Foto: Idafro/Divulgação

O Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) inaugura, nesta terça-feira (17), uma escultura de Oxê de Xangô, símbolo da Justiça na tradição iorubá e das religiões de matriz africana .

A peça foi instalada no hall do Salão Nobre, no segundo andar do edifício-sede da Corte, em Brasília , próximo ao acesso ao Plenário. A inauguração formal está prevista para o fim da tarde.

➡️ A instalação atende a um pedido do Instituto de Defesa dos Direitos das Religiões Afro-Brasileiras (Idafro) , feito em fevereiro de 2025, depois que o próprio Supremo decidiu que a presença de símbolos religiosos em prédios públicos não viola a laicidade do Estado .

Para lideranças dos povos de terreiro, a chegada do símbolo ao mais alto tribunal do país representa uma conquista histórica e o reconhecimento de tradições religiosas que foram perseguidas e ainda enfrentam preconceito no Brasil.

"É preciso que esse reconhecimento contemple também outras formas de manifestação religiosa. O crucifixo está presente na história institucional brasileira desde a colonização; reconhecer essa presença, sem abrir espaço para outras tradições, deixaria incompleta a mensagem de pluralidade", disse o babalorixá, escritor e intelectual Sidnei Nogueira de Xangô ao g1.

Para Sidnei, a presença do Oxê também representa a possibilidade de levar os conhecimentos das religiões de matriz africana para além dos terreiros.

Segundo ele, essas tradições têm formas próprias de pensar a justiça, a educação, a saúde e o cuidado em comunidade, que não devem ser tratadas como folclore.

A inauguração ocorre durante a Semana Nacional da Consciência Negra, três dias antes do feriado de 20 de novembro.

Na tradição iorubá, Xangô é o orixá associado à justiça, à autoridade e ao equilíbrio . O Oxê, também conhecido como Ọ̀sẹ́, é um bastão ritual que, em muitas representações, traz um machado de duas lâminas.

O objeto é um dos emblemas de Xangô e está associado à tradição dos povos iorubás da África Ocidental. Segundo Sidnei, a forma também tem relação histórica com o antigo reino de Ọ̀yọ́, na atual Nigéria.

O símbolo representa a necessidade de considerar os diferentes lados de um conflito antes de tomar uma decisão, sem favorecer previamente nenhuma das partes.

O babalorixá Sidnei de Xangô, que participou da articulação para a instalação da escultura ao lado do Idafro e de outras lideranças religiosas, explicou que o significado do objeto vai além de sua representação física.

"Essa forma também revela uma concepção fundamental de justiça: ela não pertence a apenas um dos lados. Suas duas lâminas nos lembram que todo conflito, desafio ou problema precisa ser observado a partir de ambos os lados. A justiça não pode chegar inclinada, favorecendo previamente uma das partes: precisa encontrar seu centro, como uma balança que só cumpre sua função quando está em equilíbrio", explicou.

Segundo Sidnei, a simbologia também carrega uma reflexão sobre a responsabilidade de quem julga. "Isso não quer dizer que os lados sejam sempre iguais ou que todas as situações tenham o mesmo peso. Quer dizer que a justiça precisa escutar, considerar os elementos do conflito e avaliar suas consequências antes de julgar", completou.

Para o babalorixá, a presença do Oxê no STF também deve provocar uma reflexão sobre as desigualdades históricas da sociedade brasileira.

"A presença do Oxê pode fazer uma pergunta ao Supremo: como construir justiça levando em conta as desigualdades que já existem antes de uma decisão ser tomada? Justiça não é apenas aplicar uma regra de modo abstrato. É também reconhecer que a sociedade brasileira foi construída por relações históricas de poder, que produziram privilégios para alguns e desproteção para muitos", afirmou.

Ele também defendeu que o reconhecimento institucional seja acompanhado de medidas concretas de proteção às comunidades religiosas.

A mãe de santo Mãe Tathy de Oyá classificou a instalação da escultura como uma conquista coletiva dos povos de terreiro.

Para ela, a presença do Oxê no STF tem um significado que ultrapassa a religião e reforça a participação das tradições de matriz africana na formação da sociedade brasileira.

"Desde sempre nossas tradições foram perseguidas, nossos símbolos demonizados e nossos espaços de culto, violentados. Estar ali, neste momento, é reafirmar que também somos parte da construção deste país, de sua cultura e de sua história", disse.

Mãe Tathy também chamou atenção para o impacto do reconhecimento sobre as novas gerações. Segundo ela, muitas crianças de terreiro ainda crescem com medo de falar sobre a própria religião fora das comunidades.

"Quando uma criança de terreiro vê um símbolo de sua ancestralidade reconhecido em uma instituição como o STF, ela recebe uma mensagem importante: sua fé também merece respeito", completou.

A mãe de santo avalia, no entanto, que a presença da escultura, sozinha, não é suficiente para combater a intolerância religiosa. " Não basta que o Estado reconheça nossos símbolos. É necessário que também proteja nossos corpos, nossas comunidades e nossos territórios", afirmou.

Decisão do STF abriu caminho para instalação

A instalação da escultura é um desdobramento de uma decisão tomada pelo Supremo Tribunal Federal em novembro de 2024.

Na ocasião, os ministros decidiram, por unanimidade, que a presença de símbolos religiosos em prédios e órgãos públicos não viola a laicidade do Estado nem a liberdade religiosa.

O julgamento ocorreu após um recurso do Ministério Público Federal que defendia a retirada desses símbolos de repartições públicas.

A Corte entendeu que a presença de representações religiosas também está relacionada à formação histórica e cultural do Brasil.

No próprio Plenário do STF, uma cruz associada à tradição católica fica posicionada na parede atrás da cadeira do presidente da Corte.

Após a decisão, o Idafro solicitou a instalação de um símbolo das religiões de matriz africana no tribunal, como forma de ampliar a representatividade religiosa no espaço.

Para Sidnei, a laicidade do Estado não significa excluir manifestações religiosas, mas garantir que diferentes tradições tenham o mesmo respeito e reconhecimento.

"O Estado laico não é um Estado contrário às religiões. É aquele que deve garantir a liberdade de todas elas, sem estabelecer privilégios ou discriminações. Proteger inclusive os direitos do ateu", afirmou.

Ele espera que a presença do Oxê também sirva como um lembrete sobre o papel da Justiça na vida cotidiana . "Que Xangô não seja apenas reconhecido nas paredes da Justiça, mas que a justiça também alcance os terreiros, as comunidades e todos aqueles que ainda precisam lutar pelo direito de exercer sua fé", concluiu.

articles.title: Acidente na Anhanguera com ambulância causa congestionamento | G1
articles.standfirst: Colisão aconteceu no Km 106, na pista sentido capital; um terceiro veículo envolvido deixou o local; Autoban informa que não houve vítimas no acidente.
articles.summary: Colisão aconteceu no Km 106, na pista sentido capital; um terceiro veículo envolvido deixou o local; Autoban informa que não houve vítimas no acidente.
articles.body:
Acidente com carreta e ambulância e causa 6 km de congestionamento na Anhanguera — Foto: Arquivo pessoal

Um acidente envolvendo uma carreta, uma ambulância do Samu e um terceiro veículo provocou 6 quilômetros de congestionamento na Rodovia Anhanguera (SP-330), em Sumaré (SP), na tarde desta terça-feira (17).

Segundo a Autoban, concessionária responsável pelo trecho, o acidente ocorreu por volta das 17h14, na altura do Km 106, no sentido capital.

Ainda de acordo com a concessionária, o terceiro veículo envolvido não foi identificado e deixou o local após a colisão.

Em nota, a Autoban afirmou que não houve vítimas em decorrência da ocorrência .

"Os veículos foram deslocados para o acostamento e, no momento, não há mais interferências no local", disse a concessionária.

articles.title: Vítimas de violência poderão receber bolsa para cursar faculdade em MS | G1
articles.standfirst: Um dos projetos encaminhado pelo governo à Assembleia prevê o pagamento adicional de R$ 300 mensais às mulheres que ingressarem na Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA), além dos R$ 450 já recebidos pelo Mais Social.
articles.summary: Um dos projetos encaminhado pelo governo à Assembleia prevê o pagamento adicional de R$ 300 mensais às mulheres que ingressarem na Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA).
articles.body:
Mulher sendo ouvida no CEAMCA, local onde atendimento integral é oferecido para as mulheres vítimas de violência. — Foto: Bruno Rezende.

O pacote de projetos de lei apresentado pelo governador Eduardo Riedel (PP) para a nova fase de sua gestão prevê a criação e ampliação de benefícios destinados a mulheres vítimas de violência em Mato Grosso do Sul.

As medidas buscam contribuir para a independência financeira das vítimas e reduzir a dependência econômica dos agressores, apontada como um dos fatores que dificultam o rompimento do ciclo de violência. Neste sentido, as propostas buscam aumentar a capacitação profissional das vítimas através dos estudos.

🔎 Os projetos foram apenas apresentados e ainda precisam ser analisados e votados pelos deputados estaduais. Para entrar em vigor, as propostas devem passar por duas votações na Assembleia Legislativa e, depois, seguir para sanção ou veto do governador.

O governo propõe reservar 600 vagas adicionais no programa MS Supera exclusivamente para mulheres vítimas de violência doméstica, conforme a secretária de Estado de Assistência Social e dos Direitos Humanos (Sead), Patrícia Cozzolino.

O MS Supera oferece auxílio mensal equivalente a um salário mínimo para estudantes do ensino superior.

“Para que essa mulher que sofreu violência doméstica possa cursar o ensino superior, recebendo um salário mínimo mensal e, assim, quebrar o ciclo da violência e se libertar dessa situação”, explicou a secretária durante coletiva de imprensa ao lado do governador, nesta terça-feira (17).

Governador ao lado dos secretários estaduais durante coletiva de imprensa, nesta terça-feira (17). — Foto: Saul Schramm.

Entre as propostas ainda está a ampliação do apoio financeiro a mulheres beneficiárias do programa Mais Social que desejam retomar os estudos. Atualmente, 95% dos beneficiários do programa são mulheres, segundo dados apresentados pela Secretaria de Estado de Assistência Social e dos Direitos Humanos (Sead).

A proposta prevê o pagamento adicional de R$ 300 mensais às mulheres que ingressarem na Educação de Jovens e Adultos (EJA), além dos R$ 450 já recebidos pelo Mais Social. Inicialmente, a medida será direcionada às beneficiárias que precisam concluir o ensino fundamental.

“Ela vai receber esses R$ 300 mensais para que consiga elevar o nível de escolaridade e se habilitar às vagas de emprego disponíveis, que têm sido anunciadas diuturnamente no estado”, disse a secretária.

Outra mudança envolve o programa Criança na Creche, que paga R$ 600 mensais para auxiliar mães de crianças de zero a três anos a custear vagas na rede privada de educação infantil quando não há disponibilidade na rede pública.

Pelo projeto, as beneficiárias poderão continuar recebendo o auxílio mesmo quando também forem contempladas pelo Benefício de Prestação Continuada (BPC).

"Programas de apoio, como à mulher trabalhadora e chefe de família, terão ajustes, pois elas precisam de suporte para evoluir em estrutura familiar", comentou Patrícia.

As iniciativas de proteção às mulheres integram um conjunto de sete projetos de lei voltados à reformulação de programas sociais de combate à pobreza e de atendimento a pessoas em situação de vulnerabilidade no estado. As propostas também contemplam jovens e adolescentes que vivem em unidades de acolhimento.

Apoio a jovens que deixam unidades de acolhimento

Um dos projetos prevê a criação do programa Recomeços Adolescentes e Jovens, destinado a pessoas que vivem em unidades de acolhimento ou com famílias acolhedoras.

A partir dos 16 anos, os adolescentes poderão participar de cursos profissionalizantes escolhidos de acordo com suas aptidões e interesses. A proposta também prevê o pagamento mensal de R$ 450, valor equivalente ao benefício do Mais Social.

Ao completarem 18 anos e deixarem as unidades de acolhimento, os jovens poderão receber acompanhamento da assistência social para alugar e mobiliar uma residência, além de apoio financeiro para iniciar a vida independente.

Ao todo, o pacote apresentado pelo governador e encaminhado à Assembleia Legislativa de Mato Grosso do Sul (Alems), nesta terça-feira (17), reúne 26 projetos de lei. As propostas serão analisadas e votadas pelos deputados estaduais. Depois, os textos retornarão ao governador, que poderá sancionar ou vetar as medidas.

articles.title: Ataque hacker afeta quase 200 sites, incluindo BBC, IKEA e Air France; criminosos tentavam roubar dados bancários | G1
articles.standfirst: O ataque tinha como objetivo roubar números de cartões de crédito e informações sobre criptomoedas dos usuários, além de instalar código malicioso em dispositivos da Apple.
articles.summary: O ataque tinha como objetivo roubar números de cartões de crédito e informações sobre criptomoedas dos usuários, além de instalar código malicioso em dispositivos da Apple.
articles.body:
Cybercrime; hacker; crimes digitais; crimes virtuais — Foto: Kevin Horvart/Unplash

Quase 200 sites, incluindo páginas da rede britânica BBC, do banco HSBC nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, da IKEA e da Air France , foram alvo de um ciberataque que buscava roubar informações financeiras e infectar dispositivos Apple, informou a imprensa especializada nesta terça-feira (17).

Hackers inseriram códigos JavaScript maliciosos em ferramentas hospedadas na Optimizely, uma plataforma digital utilizada por grandes empresas para personalizar a experiência online dos usuários. Cerca de 178 páginas foram afetadas, segundo o site especializado Cybernews.

O ataque tinha como objetivo roubar números de cartões de crédito e informações sobre criptomoedas dos usuários, além de instalar código malicioso em dispositivos da Apple.

"A lista inclui alguns dos sites mais visitados do mundo: Zoom, BBC, CNN, Salesforce, GitLab, IKEA, HSBC (Emirados Árabes Unidos), Equifax, Air France-KLM, Ledger e Peacock", escreveu na segunda-feira (16), em seu blog, o pesquisador de segurança Scott Helme, que descobriu o ataque.

"As carteiras (de criptomoedas) dos invasores receberam cerca de 7.040 dólares (R$ 40 mil), em um período de aproximadamente nove horas, no dia 16 de novembro", acrescentou.

A maior parte do código foi removida dos sites afetados, afirmou Helme.

articles.title: North Korea’s Kim Jong Un inspects ski resort as rumors of Trump meeting swirl
articles.summary: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected construction of a tourism zone near the Chinese border, state media reported, amid speculation over a China trip.
articles.body: North Korean leader Kim Jong Un inspected construction of a tourism zone near the Chinese border in recent days, state media KCNA reported on Tuesday, amid speculation over a China trip fueled by comments from U.S. and Russian officials. Kim toured the Samjiyon airport reconstruction, a tourist railway line and a ski resort on Sunday and Monday, and pronounced the resort’s hotels, lodges and housing flawless and worthy of top marks, KCNA said. The visit comes amid renewed speculation over whether the secretive North Korean leader might travel abroad after President Donald Trump said on Monday he might meet Kim in China this week. Russia’s Interfax also quoted Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov as saying that President Vladimir Putin could meet Kim if the North Korean leader also attended this week’s Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen. KCNA photographs showed Kim, alongside his daughter Ju Ae, touring hotels and inspecting facilities near a snow-capped hillside. Dressed in white, Ju Ae was seen skiing down a slope. South Korean intelligence believes she is being groomed as Kim’s successor. Kim ordered that the airport’s runway extension meet International Civil Aviation Organization standards, KCNA said. He also climbed Mount Paektu to review a rebuilt cable car station and work near Heaven Lake, demanding the highest quality for every structure there, KCNA said. Separately, Jo Yong Won, a member of the Presidium of the Political Bureau and secretary of the Central Committee of North Korea’s ruling Workers’ Party, met Putin, the Interfax and TASS news agencies reported. Addressing a Moscow forum on Monday, Jo said the security environment around North Korea was being pushed towards danger by Washington’s “inveterate hostile policy” towards Pyongyang, according to KCNA. South Korea’s Unification Ministry noted on Monday the North Korean delegation, which had been in Russia since November 14, had travelled shortly before a U.S.-China-Russia summit scheduled for this week in China, and said it would monitor developments. Meanwhile, Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Monday that Russia was receiving new supplies of “dozens” of North Korean ballistic missiles each month, citing an intelligence report.

articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) on Tuesday hit back at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi over his remarks that fear, anger and hatred had created a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters, asking him to identify those responsible for the destruction of the historic Hoysala capital of Halebidu in Karnataka.Responding to Rahul's post on X, the BJP questioned his use of the phrase “Satyam Shivam Sundaram” and referred to the history of the Hoysala capital, which was ransacked during invasions in the 14th century.“Mr Gandhi, since you've posted Halebidu, a few questions,” the party said while retweeting his post.The BJP asked Rahul whether he knew why Dwarasamudra, the former Hoysala capital, came to be known as Halebidu, meaning the "old capital”.“Can you bring yourself to name who ransacked it? We can: Alauddin Khalji's general Malik Kafur in 1311, and Muhammad bin Tughlaq's army in 1326-27. Can you shame them?” the party said.Referring to the damaged sculptures at the Hoysaleshwara Temple complex, it added, “Across Halebidu, Idols of gods still stand with broken faces and hands. Who broke them?”“Satyam comes first in Satyam Shivam Sundaram, RaGa. Did you know?” the BJP added.The exchange followed Rahul's post on X earlier on Tuesday, in which he hit back at BJP and RSS supporters amid the controversy over his remarks about his parents' relationship. He said fear, anger and hatred had prevented them from experiencing and expressing love.“Fear, anger and hatred have woven a web in the hearts of BJP and RSS supporters that stops them from experiencing and expressing love,” the Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha said.“As a true Hindu, it is my duty to free them from this web, so that they too can start to experience the breathtaking beauty and joy of love and belonging in their lives,” he added, ending his post with “Satyam Shivam Sundaram”.The sculpture at the Hoysaleshwara Temple in Halebidu that Rahul referred to depicts Lord Shiva and Goddess Parvati riding Nandi, Shiva's sacred bull.Assam Chief Minister Himanta Biswa Sarma also criticised Rahul's post, saying no human being, including anyone from the Gandhi family, could be equated with God."To portray mortals as Shiv and Parvati is not devotion. articles.title: Henry Nowak killer applies to appeal against conviction
articles.summary: Vicrum Digwa, who fatally stabbed Nowak in Southampton in 2015, is also seeking a sentence review.
articles.body:
The man jailed for murdering Henry Nowak has applied to appeal against his conviction.

Vickrum Digwa, who stabbed the 18-year-old student with a large dagger in Belmont Road, Southampton, on 3 December 2025, has also asked the Supreme Court to review his sentence, his lawyers have confirmed.

Earlier this month the Court of Appeal raised his minimum term from 21 to 25 years , after the Attorney General argued it was unduly lenient.

The BBC understands Digwa wants to argue that his conviction for murder is unsafe on four grounds. The applications do not mean Digwa will automatically get any further hearings or reviews.

Imran Khan and Partners, Digwa's lawyers, said: "An application has been lodged seeking to appeal against Vickrum Singh Digwa's conviction.

"That application concerns the safety of the conviction and is separate from the proceedings concerning sentence."

Nowak, from Chafford Hundred in Essex, was stabbed to death with a 21cm (8in) kirpan, a religious blade that Digwa said he carried as part of his Sikh faith.

Digwa, then 22, told police that Nowak had attacked and racially abused him, which led to him being handcuffed as he lay dying.

The Court of Appeal ruling included a finding that Nowak had not threatened Digwa and Digwa was responsible for the first act of force by snatching Henry's phone.

Digwa then filmed Nowak as he lay bleeding on the ground and the ruling noted that in the video, Nowak can be heard denying that he had racially abused him.

The trial judge later found Digwa's claims of racism to be a lie and there was no evidence Nowak was racist.

Digwa was jailed for life at Southampton Crown Court in June with a minimum term of 21 years.

One of the four grounds on which Digwa plans to challenge his murder conviction is that the trial judge wrongly excluded from evidence WhatsApp messages Nowak sent when he was about 13, which Digwa suggested displayed a history of racist language.

The messages were found by police during their review of Nowak's phone but the judge ruled them irrelevant and inadmissible.

Digwa is also seeking to appeal his conviction on the basis the jury should not have been told that police had secretly recorded him confessing to the stabbing.

The recording, he argues, breaks evidence rules relating to such material.

On 5 November, the Court of Appeal ruled that the trial judge had been right to calculate Digwa's minimum term from a starting point of 15 years as there had been no evidence he had planned to use the knife as a weapon.

Had that been the case, the starting point under sentencing law for murder would have been 25 years.

But the Lady Chief Justice Baroness Carr said the final figure of 21 years had been too low because it understated Digwa's repeated use of the knife and the "deliberate cruelty, additional suffering and obstruction" that followed.

She and two other senior judges ordered "a very significant uplift ... to reflect the use of the large kirpan alone" and extended the minimum term to 25 years.

Digwa and his lawyers are seeking a review of how the judges reached that figure.

"The Court of Appeal upheld the sentencing judge's finding that Vickrum Singh Digwa had not taken the kirpan to the scene intending to commit an offence or intending to have it available for use as a weapon," his lawyers said in a statement.

"The court nevertheless concluded that the circumstances surrounding the weapon justified a very significant uplift and ultimately substituted a 25-year minimum term.

"The application therefore raises an issue of wider importance."

The Supreme Court reviews relatively few criminal cases and only does so where a point of law is disputed and it has wider implications for other cases.

articles.title: FAA pauses router upgrades linked to nationwide ground stop
articles.summary: The agency says it has paused installing Juniper routers after Democratic lawmakers asked it to do so.
articles.body:
The United States Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) has disabled potentially faulty functionality in its telecommunications network and halted the installation of new routers linked with a national ground stop last week.

“We believe we have addressed the initial cause of the disruption by immediately disabling the functionality of the originating Juniper routers,” the agency said on its website on Tuesday.

“As a precaution, we disabled the same functionality on more than 60 other Juniper routers in the system, and we have paused installing them.”

A group of Democratic senators had asked the FAA to pause its plan to replace thousands of routers until an investigation is completed into why one such upgrade caused a national ground stop last week.

“With thousands of conversions remaining, FAA must address outstanding ‌‌safety ‌‌and reliability concerns before expanding installation,” the 13 senators wrote in a letter to the agency earlier in the day.

The FAA ordered all flights to remain grounded on Friday for about four hours, causing more than 10,000 flights to be cancelled and prompting ripple effects that continue to disrupt air travel in the US. It was only the second time the agency had issued such a sweeping order since the September 11, 2001 attacks.

The FAA said in a statement on Sunday that its initial investigation pointed to upgrades at two locations – a radar site in Amarillo, Texas, and a radio communications site in El Dorado, Arkansas – as being the cause of the problem.

L3Harris, the agency’s network service provider, had been working to replace old copper wires with fibre-optic lines and to replace old routers with new ones made by Juniper Networks.

The FBI said on Tuesday that it was working with the Department of Transportation, the FAA, and L3Harris to investigate the incident, but had not taken possession of any equipment itself.

In their letter to the FAA, the group of senators asked the agency to halt plans to replace more than 3,000 additional routers.

“Based on information ⁠⁠provided to our offices from L3Harris, the copper-to-fibre transition involves converting 3,648 routers to Juniper ⁠⁠devices. To date, it is our understanding that ⁠⁠400 devices have ⁠⁠been installed, and 69 are operational,” wrote the lawmakers from the Senate Commerce Committee, ‌‌led by Maria Cantwell.

On Sunday, the FAA said the upgrades had started a long time ago.

“This type of work has been going on for years to transition from old copper wires that are being disconnected due to their obsolescence,” the FAA said on Sunday.

During Friday’s mass ground stop, the FAA said its system became “unstable” as a result of an upgrade, and data began flooding other equipment, causing problems with aircraft communications and radar feeds.

That led the agency to order a nationwide halt to outbound flights out of an “abundance of caution”.

“I want the American people to know my number one job is to keep them safe,” Secretary of Transportation Sean Duffy told ABC on Sunday. “So if we see these inconsistencies in the network, whether it’s communication with air traffic controllers and pilots, or with data feeds, we’re going to keep you safe.”

The White House has asked Congress for $50bn to complete an overhaul of the FAA’s technical infrastructure.

Democratic lawmakers have resisted that request, though, arguing that the administration was already authorised to use $12.5bn last year — but has only used a fraction of that sum so far.

articles.title: Fraud lawsuit against Selena Gomez’s mental health company voluntarily dropped
articles.summary: A lawsuit filed against Selena Gomez’s mental health startup, Wondermind, has been voluntarily dismissed, according to court documents.
articles.body: A lawsuit filed against Selena Gomez’s mental health startup, Wondermind, has been voluntarily dismissed, according to court documents. Investors filed suit against Wondermind in August, alleging they were misled into investing $1.2 million in the company, which launched in 2021, after being given false promises about its leadership, resources and infrastructure for years. Weeks later, Gomez filed an appeal, asking that the case against her and her company be dismissed. Gomez announced Wondermind alongside her mother, Mandy Teefey, and their former business partner, Daniella Pierson, in late 2021. All three, along with Wondermind, are listed as defendants in the suit alleging common-law fraud, breach of contract and securities fraud. But plaintiffs opted to dismiss the suit, according to a filing in federal court in Delaware on Monday. The suit was dismissed with prejudice, meaning it cannot be brought again. It was not immediately clear why the lawsuit was tossed. Lawyers for the investors — Wondermind SRS 44 LLC and Bespoke Wondermind SPV I LLC — did not immediately respond to requests for comment. A lawyer for Gomez did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Teefy also did not immediately respond to a request for comment. Pierson, who has previously denied the allegations, also did not respond to a request for comment. In the initial suit, investors alleged that the founders told them the “mental fitness” company would include a phone app, advertising deals and celebrity-driven content, including from Gomez. But they alleged that many of those promises never materialized. Investors said they were given false updates and were kept in the dark about the company’s management practices and finances, according to the suit. They said they only learned about the company’s troubles after two articles about it were published in Forbes and The Cut, according to the suit. “The notion that Selena engaged in ‘fraud’ or any other wrongdoing is absurd,” Mathew S. Rosengart, an attorney for Gomez, said in a statement following the appeal in August. In the motion for appeal, Gomez’s attorneys argued that Gomez herself never made any of the false statements specified in the lawsuit and that she was not even a member of Wondermind’s board. She also never agreed to manage the company and did not hold a minority stake in it, the appeal said. It added that Teefy and Pierson handled company management as co-CEOs and board members and that Gomez served as “a consultant and conferred on her title of Chief Impact Officer.” Wondermind, which describes itself on its website as an “easy, inclusive space where people could come together to explore, discuss, and navigate their feelings,” appears to still be up and running, but its social media pages have been relatively inactive recently. Gomez, a global pop star and actor, also helms Rare Beauty, a multibillion-dollar makeup and skincare brand.

articles.title: Trump announces critical minerals agreements at Quad meeting in Manila
articles.summary: US President Trump says the deals will prevent ‘coercion by any single foreign supplier’.
articles.body:
United States President Donald Trump says that members of the Quad, a security grouping of the US and three Indo-Pacific countries, have reached agreements aimed at securing supply chains of critical minerals .

Trump met India’s Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Australia’s Prime Minister Anthony Albanese and Japan’s Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi – the other Quad leaders – in the Philippines on Thursday.

“Our countries are the four corners of a free, open, stable, and prosperous Indo-Pacific,” Trump said in remarks ahead of the meeting in Manila.

During the meeting, Trump said the agreements on critical minerals aimed to prevent “coercion by any single foreign supplier”. He did not single out China, which dominates global rare earth supplies .

Trump later said the US would have “everything we need” on rare earths in 10 months.

“We are making rare earth at a level that we’ve never made before. We’re going to catch them [China] within 10 months,” he said.

China last year imposed restrictions on exports of rare earths amid a trade dispute with the US. In June, the two sides agreed a deal aimed at restoring the US’s access to China’s rare earth supplies.

In a statement after the leaders’ meeting, the Quad expressed “grave concerns” about “economic coercion”, including through arbitrary export restrictions.

While the statement did not name any country, the US and Japan have complained about China’s restrictions on ‌exports of rare earths vital to the manufacturing of everything from electric cars to mobile phones.

China has effectively shut off exports of key critical minerals to Japan for nearly a year as relations between Asia’s two largest economies have nosedived.

It was Trump’s first meeting of the Quad grouping – which his predecessor US President Joe Biden regarded as a signature foreign policy initiative.

Scott Lucas, professor of international politics at the Clinton Institute at University College Dublin, told Al Jazeera that the meeting suggested the Quad grouping had a “functioning relationship”.

“Given the damage to the Quad during the Trump administration, including the instability caused by Trump’s tariffs on India, and India’s response by diversifying, the Quad meeting and statements like this give reassurance that there is still a functioning relationship,” Lucas said. “I’m not sure I’d call it an alliance, as I don’t think the Trump folks believe in alliances.”

Trump also joined a summit of the Association of Southeast Asian Nations in Manila on the first day of a three-day trip to Asia.

After the Philippines, Trump will travel to China and attend the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation forum in Shenzhen, where he is expected to hold a trilateral meeting with Russian President Vladimir Putin and Chinese President Xi Jinping on Thursday.

The Chinese Ministry of Foreign Affairs says the talks will focus on topics of “groundbreaking significance”, including “safeguarding world peace”.

Asked by reporters about a CNN report which claimed that US intelligence had determined Tehran was developing plans to use a so-called “dirty bomb” to target officials in the Trump administration, Trump said he was “looking into it”.

He said that if Iran posed an “imminent threat” to Washington, “they will pay a price the likes of which no country has ever paid before”.

He added that he “hoped” Iran did not pose a threat, but that he took such a scenario “very seriously” because “they happen to be crazy”.

Iranian Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghei said in a post on X that “Those who initiated the aggression against Iran are now seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs by manufacturing and disseminating baseless allegations, including the recent claims published by The New York Times and the fabricated media narrative surrounding an alleged ‘dirty bomb’ propagated by CNN.”

articles.title: In 2015, China replaced 20 cm of lime-stabilised soil beneath a 4.9-km expressway section with modified aluminium-industry waste; field tests measured a resilient modulus above 90 MPa and core samples recorded an average compressive strength of 2.4 MPa
articles.summary: Discover how China transformed industrial waste into a viable road construction material, enhancing resilience and environmental safety in the Ji-Qing Expressway project.
articles.body: A closer look at the road surface shows a fresh underlay of modified red mud, a byproduct of aluminium production that was once difficult to store. Replaced a traditional soil layer along a 4.9 km stretch of the Ji-Qing Expressway reconstruction project. Field testing of the material used to replace the traditional soil layer found it had a higher resilient modulus of over 90 MPa and an average compression strength of 2.4 MPa. The stretch of road was built in 2015, and the study published by the Shandong Transportation Research Institute showed how troublesome industrial byproducts could be turned into a viable road construction material.How aluminium industry waste became a road construction material Red mud, also known as bauxite residue, is waste that forms after the extraction of alumina from bauxite ore. This material contains several metal oxides, such as iron oxide, aluminium oxide, and silicon dioxide. While there is potential to reuse this waste material in various industries, its inherent characteristics as industrial waste make it difficult for direct use in the construction of roads. The waste material has high moisture content, small particle size, low water stability, and high water alkalinity, which gives rise to concern regarding the potential transfer of certain chemicals to the environment.The study also estimates that around 1 to 1.8 tonnes of red mud are produced for every tonne of alumina through the Bayer process. The researchers looked for ways to solve the problems and developed a chemical modification method using cement, phosphogypsum, and a polymer stabiliser. The mixture was able to bind the small particles, strengthen the material, and limit the transfer of dangerous substances. The team tested different amounts of the mixture ranging from 4 to 12% of the weight of the red mud. They found that the optimal dose is around 8%, resulting in the material reaching a compressive strength of 3 megapascals after three days of curing.A 4.9-kilometre expressway section puts the material to the testThis was demonstrated during the reconstruction and widening of the Ji-Qing Highway in Shandong Province. The existing four-lane road was expanded to eight lanes to accommodate increasing traffic volume. A test was selected between K289+090.5 and K294+385, with K289+090.5 marking the beginning section. The road was about 4900 m long, 11 m wide, and had a modified red mud filling thickness of 20 cm. The material replaced the lime-stabilised soil layer in this section.The mixture was not designed on the road, but at a central plant. The treated residue was delivered to the site and spread over the prepared surface using vibrating equipment, then compacted. Once the final compaction and curing were completed by the workers, the next layer of construction was laid. Quality control was a concern because varying levels of moisture content and the dosage of the modified agent used could have an impact on the strength of the treated residue, and the construction standard stipulated that the mixture should be compacted within four hours of mixing. The surface also had to be covered or watered during the curing process.Field results highlight strength and environmental considerationsAfter seven days of moist curing, the roadbed was tested with a bearing plate test, a portable falling-weight device, and a falling-weight deflectometer. All but one of the measuring points showed a resilient modulus greater than 90 MPa. The dynamic deformation modulus was greater than 140 MPa, and the deflection was less than 100 units of 0.01 millimetres. This suggested that the modified material would provide sufficient support for the road. Samples from the finished section were then subjected to more compaction tests. The average unconfined compressive strength of the samples was 2.4 MPa, with the lowest value being 2.06 MPa and the highest 2.77 MPa, all within the estimated 95% confidence interval.Environmental monitoring was also a key part of the test. Four groundwater monitoring wells were installed around the demonstration sections, and samples were taken both before and after construction. The pH of the monitored groundwater eventually remained between 7 and 8, and the concentration of various potentially harmful materials remained below the relevant limits, with no deviation from the red mud section. The findings are consistent with wider research into the reuse of industrial residue in infrastructure. A review published in Minerals also demonstrated the use of treated red mud in road applications to help meet the required earthworks specification in place of using ordinary soil and other natural materials. This also provided an economic incentive for usage.In the study by the institute, applying locally treated red mud to compacted earthworks resulted in savings of about 10 yuan per ton of compacted earthworks as opposed to using ordinary lime and cement-stabilised soil, over a distance between 15 and 20 km. This does not mean untreated red mud can be used on highways, because its chemical properties, stability, and environmental impacts still need thorough evaluation. articles.title: Louisiana residents want Amazon’s 80-pound delivery drones out of their sky; Amazon says: We believe customers in suburban and semirural areas should...
articles.summary: Amazon’s Prime Air delivery drones have been flying over Baton Rouge, Louisiana, since July, and more and more residents want them out of their sky.
articles.body: Amazon’s Prime Air delivery drones have been flying over Baton Rouge, Louisiana, since July, and more and more residents want them out of their sky. Locals say the 80-pound drones sound like flying leaf blowers and fly barely above the treetops. They also say the drones raise privacy concerns and may be driving away birds. Marcia LeCompte counted 18 of them on one dog walk and compared it to “living under an overpass.” Her husband Rick told The Wall Street Journal: “They’re stealing the sky.”Amazon isn’t backing down. “We believe customers in suburban and semirural areas should have access to fast delivery,” spokeswoman Lindsay Hamilton said. She added that delivery slots fill almost as soon as they open.Baton Rouge residents say Amazon drones are louder than a vacuum cleanerTempers flared at a packed meeting at Broadmoor Methodist Church in October. Residents asked Amazon representatives why the drones flew so low, what happens to the camera footage and whether wildlife was being harmed. Michael Cole, who designs sound equipment, said he measured drones over his backyard at up to 87 decibels. Bob Storer counted 18 flyovers in 21 minutes on a Sunday morning.Amazon has since raised flying heights and spread out its routes. Many residents report quieter skies, though some say other areas now see more drones. About 30 drones an hour leave the hub, carrying packages of up to 5 pounds to homes within 7.5 miles. Amazon says its drones don’t use facial recognition or record audio, and employees don’t watch live feeds. It says it shares images with government agencies, including police, only when the law requires it or to protect public safety.Amazon’s drone delivery expansion is meeting resistance beyond LouisianaSome locals are fans. Councilman Cleve Dunn Jr. pointed out that Amazon invested $200 million in the fulfilment centre and created 2,000 jobs. The centre was built where a mall used to stand. Monica Anderson says her kids are disappointed when a drone drops a package while they’re at school.The pushback is growing along with Prime Air. The service flies from 18 sites in 10 states, and Amazon plans to reach 500 cities and towns this year. Residents near Richardson, Texas, have formed an opposition group called Quiet Skies Texas. In Westborough, Massachusetts, local opposition led Amazon to withdraw its drone programme before it got off the ground. The ACLU’s Jay Stanley told WSJ the big question is whether Americans want this at all.For some critics, the answer isn’t simple. Kay Radlauer, who now logs drones from a backyard she planted for hummingbirds and woodpeckers, said: “We’re not a bunch of revolutionaries. We’re people that use Amazon Prime.”Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.

articles.summary: Andrew Kozak, the BioUrja worker accused in the Peoria bomb threat, has a criminal past spanning four Nebraska counties, Fox News Digital reports.
articles.body: An Illinois ethanol plant worker with a lengthy criminal past was federally indicted Tuesday after prosecutors said he emailed a threat claiming explosive devices had been placed at the facility where he worked. A federal grand jury indicted Andrew M. Kozak on Tuesday on charges of threats regarding explosives and interstate communications of a threat. Prosecutors allege Kozak emailed BioUrja Renewables on Friday indicating that explosive devices had been placed at the company's Peoria facility. LIVE EXPLOSIVE DEVICE FOUND NEAR HOMELAND SECURITY OFFICE IN CLEVELAND, FORCING MASS EVACUATIONS The email threatened to damage and destroy a building and other property "by means of fire and an explosive," according to the indictment. NBC Chicago previously reported that Kozak, 41, of Chillicothe, had worked at BioUrja for about 10 months and allegedly planted the explosive device before sending the threat, citing federal law enforcement sources. The indictment does not accuse Kozak of physically planting the explosive device found at the facility. During a news conference Tuesday, federal officials declined to say who built or planted the explosive device, how many devices were involved or how powerful the device was. They also would not say whether anyone else may have been involved. FBI Springfield Special Agent in Charge Ryan Presley said most bomb threats investigated by law enforcement are ultimately deemed not credible. "But in this instance, it was," Presley said. "Had it not been for the swift action of the responders and the bomb technicians, this incident could have had a very different outcome." Peoria Police Chief Brad Dixon said about 2,500 homes were evacuated as authorities responded to the threat. Kozak returned to BioUrja for work Monday morning and was taken into custody when he arrived, NBC Chicago reported, citing federal sources. FBI agents also executed a search warrant at his Chillicothe home, according to the outlet. Kozak has a criminal past that includes several burglary-related felony convictions across four Nebraska counties and two stints in state prison, records reviewed by Fox News Digital show. Kozak's criminal history stretches back two decades. Court and corrections records reviewed by Fox News Digital show Kozak was convicted of multiple burglary-related felonies across Platte, Polk, Nance and Colfax counties in Nebraska. In Platte County, Kozak pleaded no contest to three felony burglary charges after initially facing seven burglary counts and one attempted burglary charge. A judge found him guilty and determined Kozak was "not a fit and proper person" for probation before sentencing him to three to five years in prison. Kozak was also convicted in two Polk County felony burglary cases. One court record identifies Osceola High School, while another shows Kozak was ordered to pay restitution to Osceola Public Schools. In Nance County, Kozak was convicted of attempted felony burglary and sentenced to 20 months to five years in prison. MASSIVE CHEMICAL FIRE ERUPTS AT ELECTRICAL TRANSFORMER PLANT IN MISSISSIPPI, FORCING EVACUATION Nebraska corrections records show Kozak was released on discretionary parole in August 2008. He later returned to state prison on a separate Colfax County burglary conviction carrying a three-to-five-year sentence. Kozak was released on discretionary parole in October 2014, and his parole expired in May 2015. CAR LOADED WITH EXPLOSIVES SLAMS INTO LAVISH PORTLAND SOCIAL CLUB, BOMB SQUAD STILL PULLING OUT LIVE DEVICES The investigation began Friday afternoon when workers at BioUrja reported receiving a bomb threat. About an hour later, authorities located a suspicious package near the facility. The device was deemed a credible threat, triggering the evacuation of homes and businesses within a one-mile radius. FOLLOW THE FOX TRUE CRIME TEAM ON X "I can just tell you it was deemed a credible threat," Dixon said Saturday. "There's an extensive criminal investigation going on." Authorities warned that BioUrja houses large quantities of ethanol and other highly combustible materials, raising concerns about the potential consequences of an ignition. Bomb technicians rendered the device safe, and authorities searched the facility without finding additional suspicious devices. The evacuation order was lifted Saturday after nearly a full day. articles.title: Thousands demand cancellation of Nathan Cofnas talk at Oxford University
articles.summary: Online petition with more than 32,000 signatures demands the university ‘cancel Nathan Cofnas’s invitation to speak’.
articles.body:
Thousands of people have signed a petition and protests are planned at the University of Oxford against the appearance of Nathan Cofnas, an American academic and self-described “race realist” accused of racism.

Cofnas, who had accused the late Professor Jason Arday of plagiarism last July, is due to give a talk at Oxford’s Oriel College on Tuesday evening at an event organised by the Oxford Reform student society, which is linked to the far-right Reform UK party.

Cofnas has drawn controversy for years with his eugenics-linked views tying race to intelligence, writing that Black people were less intelligent than others in an article which led to his dismissal from his position at a college at Emmanuel College, Cambridge.

He was suspended as a postdoctoral researcher at Ghent University in Belgium in August after making plagiarism allegations against Arday, a Black Cambridge professor. Arday consistently denied allegations of plagiarism but acknowledged errors in his work.

Arday was later found dead in his home after resigning his post amid the ballooning scandal.

Cofnas was later allowed to resume some academic work at Ghent remotely, without teaching, while an investigation continued.

The Oxford Reform student society defended its event – titled “Is DEI Undermining Higher Education?”, referring to diversity, equity and inclusion – and said it is “committed to broadening participation in university life”.

In a statement, Oxford University said the event being hosted on its grounds “does not imply endorsement by the College of the views of its speakers”.

An online petition demanding the university “cancel Nathan Cofnas’s invitation to speak” has more than 32,000 signatures.

“Ideas platformed at Oxford do not stay in the lecture theatre”, the petition said.

articles.title: Brad Pitt and Florence Pugh pitch for James Bond villain role
articles.summary: The two A-list stars throw their hats into the ring to be the villain facing Robert Pattinson's 007.
articles.body:
We have barely come up for breath since Robert Pattinson was picked as the new James Bond, but A-listers are already jostling for position to play his enemy in the next 007 movie.

At the premiere of his new film in Hollywood on Monday, Brad Pitt was asked by Extra TV if he would like to play the villain in director Denis Villeneuve's forthcoming spy movie.

With a wink at the camera, the star replied: "Robert! Denis! You know, I'd like to do that. I'd be up for that. My man Javier [Bardem] did it so well. It's tall shoes, but I'd take that on."

Bardem played Bond baddie Raoul Silva in 2012's Skyfall, opposite Daniel Craig. Asked the same question by Complex later, Pitt was still enthusiastic: "Sign me up for the villain. Get Denis Villeneuve on the flip phone, let's go!"

Meanwhile, Florence Pugh, who stars alongside Pattinson in Villeneuve's forthcoming Dune: Part Three, said she had thrown her hat in the ring to be in the new Bond film upon hearing the casting news.

Speaking at Elle's Women in Hollywood event on Monday, Pugh said she had sent a message to the director saying: "Congratulations on finding your Bond, nice catch. Any villains the size of a 5ft 4in female?"

In fact, it was Villeneuve presenting Pugh with an honour at the event - so he's now heard her plea twice.

Meanwhile, Pitt also told reporters at the premiere of The Further Mis-Adventures of Cliff Booth in Los Angeles that he was delighted to hear the news about Pattinson's recruitment as 007.

"Is that right?! You know what, I love this idea," Pitt told Extra TV.

"I love what he's been doing. I love his choices, I think he's the real deal. That's great, good call."

Bond villains over the years have included Rami Malek, Jonathan Pryce, Christoph Waltz and Christopher Walken.

Several other actors have indicated they would like a shot at being a Bond baddie ahead of Pattinson's casting announcement, including Bill Skarsgård, Saoirse Ronan and Barry Keoghan.

articles.title: ICE is detaining green-card holders over decades-old, minor violations
articles.summary: In the three decades that San Juanita Guerra had been crossing into Mexico to fill prescriptions, she never had a problem returning home to the United States...
articles.body:
ICE is detaining green-card holders over decades-old, minor violations

In the three decades that San Juanita Guerra had been crossing into Mexico to fill prescriptions, she never had a problem returning home to the United States.

But last March, officers at a South Texas port of entry detained the then-74-year-old green-card holder. Border officials had taken her fingerprints and discovered a 30-year-old conviction on a weapons charge.

Guerra had no criminal record in the years since, and the misdemeanor had not prevented her from renewing her status three times. Nor had it come up during the hundreds of trips she had taken to Mexico, said her attorney, Wendoli Rodriguez.

But now legal permanent residents - immigrants granted the right to live and work indefinitely in the United States - are finding that their status is not as secure as many previously thought. Attorneys say clients are getting flagged at border crossings and airports by officers who are checking identification cards and flight manifests.

In some cases, authorities are detaining people over decades-old charges that did not come up when they applied for or renewed their green cards and that in the past would have resulted in a citation - not an effort to remove legal status.

The detentions mark a shift in how President Donald Trump's administration is treating a group of immigrants who already have undergone vetting and in many cases have lived for extended periods in the United States.

Some immigrants, like Guerra, are being accused of not disclosing the charges when they submitted that paperwork. Attorneys and relatives for several recently detained longtime permanent residents said in some cases charges had been expunged or dismissed. They say the omission was a mistake, not an attempt to commit fraud.

"I tell all my clients, if you have a green card, just stay home. Don't travel, it's not a good time for that," said Jodi Goodwin, an immigration attorney in Texas. "They will use anything to try to detain someone."

One green-card holder, Emiliano Andrade Covarrubias, died in U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement custody last month after he was stopped at a port of entry while returning to the United States from Mexico. The Department of Homeland Security accused the 56-year-old of obtaining his green card without telling U.S. Customs and Immigration Services that he had faced theft charges years earlier.

States cooperating with DHS, such as Florida and Texas, have granted the agency access to a wealth of information about its residents, handing over databases with information on criminal records, voter registrations and more. Officers use powerful surveillance, digital forensics and data-mining tools employing artificial intelligence to pinpoint information that could lead to an arrest or termination of a permanent status.

Federal agencies such as the Transportation Security Administration also are sharing information with DHS that permits officers to identify violations that could lead to a green card being revoked - such as tax evasion or staying outside the United States for more than six months.

DHS did not respond to a request for comment on how many green-card holders it has detained. The agency has argued that reviews are essential for safeguarding the country and that no noncitizen should ever feel their stay in the United States is unconditional. Port officials in Texas said they always have conducted these checks and denied following any specific directives or arrest quotas from the Trump administration.

The information that officers are using to detain people can offer an incomplete picture of what transpired in someone's past, several attorneys said.

John Gihon, a former ICE attorney who now practices immigration law in Florida, described the example of one client who has been a permanent resident for decades and accidentally registered to vote after receiving the forms in the mail. While traveling back to the United States recently, ICE detained him at the airport.

In court, Gihon demonstrated that his client had not falsely claimed to be a citizen on the voter-registration forms. The local supervisor of elections wrote a letter apologizing for mistakenly processing the registration. Gihon did not name the client, saying he wanted to protect the man's identity.

"It wasn't the crime of the century," Gihon said. "We won his case, and he kept his green card. But he didn't deserve to sleep on a pee-stained mattress in detention for weeks. That's unnecessary."

Lawful permanent residents must disclose any criminal history when seeking a green card, even if the charge ultimately was dismissed, in addition to other information such as financial records.

Attorneys and advocates said many lawful permanent residents successfully challenge their detentions in immigration court and keep their green cards. But being held for weeks or months is nonetheless challenging for both the individual and their family.

Andrade Covarrubias, the man found dead at a South Texas detention center in October, spent months fighting his case as his health deteriorated. The longtime Dallas resident obtained a green card in 2019, and ran a contracting and painting business with his son. He had been charged with theft in 2004. His daughter Estefani Andrade said he had taken a ladder after a client failed to pay him.

Monica Yoas, an ICE spokeswoman, said in a statement that Andrade Covarrubias was attempting to enter Laredo, Texas, on June 26 when agents determined he had "obtained status through fraudulent means by failing to disclose his previous arrest during the review process." She added that "He was receiving due process."

Dallas County records show the father of three pleaded no contest to the misdemeanor charge. He received deferred adjudication from the judge - meaning it did not appear as a conviction on his record. Andrade Covarrubias served probation and had the option of having the charge expunged.

Texas border attorney Jaime Diez said he has handled at least 100 cases in the last 18 months in which green-card holders were detained. In several, he said, officers acted on information that proved incorrect. He described the case of a 65-year-old woman who had gone to Mexico for a church retreat. When she returned, officers questioned whether she had registered to vote in 1995.

The woman, whom Diez declined to name, has had a green card since 1987. She was detained for 10 days, and the case against her was dismissed because officers were unable to prove that she had indeed registered.

"They are focusing on finding things to make you ineligible to stay here," he said. "And they are doing it without any consequences."

Andrade Covarrubias, who ICE said had been receiving proper care and had a "documented medical history of diabetes, hypertension, and anxiety," was found unresponsive Oct. 17 in his detention bed. He was pronounced dead moments later. Andrade said it was clear from her father's deterioration that he was not receiving adequate care or his medications regularly while detained.

"We have always felt that the circumstances surrounding his case and the way he was treated deserved to be heard," said Andrade, who helped her father complete the green-card paperwork and process as a teenager. "We don't want what happened to him to be forgotten."

In Guerra's case, the September 1994 weapons charge stemmed from a family crisis and a mistake, said her daughter Carla Gomez. One of Guerra's teenage children had been struggling with suicidal thoughts and obtained a gun. The single mother took the gun and put it in her purse, Guerra said in an interview.

Two days later, Guerra went to pick up her sister at McAllen International Airport in Texas's Rio Grande Valley. While there, airport security detected the unloaded pistol and charged her with unlawfully carrying a weapon, according to Hidalgo County court records.

Guerra said her attorney at the time advised her to plead guilty to the misdemeanor charge. She paid a fine and was briefly on probation. Then the case was dismissed.

Guerra, now 75, obtained her green card a decade before the incident with the firearm. Authorities did not terminate her status as a result of the charge, and Guerra said she mistakenly thought it had been wiped from her record. A notary public erroneously advised her that she didn't need to disclose it on future applications, she added.

But on March 2, officials at the Progreso port of entry - a popular crossing for medical tourists and day shoppers - took Guerra's fingerprints after she forgot her green card at home. One of her daughters brought the documents to the port office. They expected the matter to clear up.

But the biometric database pinged Guerra's 30-year-old conviction.

"Yo cumplí con todo. … Se lo expliqué," Guerra recalled telling the officer. "I'm done with that. … I explained what happened."

ICE officers shackled her. She spent 22 days in detention, where relatives say she didn't sleep or eat well. Guerra said younger detainees took pity on her and found extra mats to give the older woman more cushion for her ailing hip. But nothing helped. She became severely disoriented and weak.

Gomez, her daughter, said fellow detainees contacted her, saying that if she didn't get Guerra out soon, the woman would die there. The family rallied community support, an attorney immediately filed for a bond hearing, and an immigration judge granted the request.

"I had to move quickly because she was declining rapidly in detention," said Rodriguez, her attorney.

Guerra was outfitted with an ankle bracelet to track her whereabouts, though it was later removed after she raised health concerns. Her family is still trying to pay back the $15,000 they borrowed to secure her release. She has a hearing scheduled for later this month.

articles.title: UK sanctions eight Israeli firms over West Bank settlements, targets Gaza aid-blocking group
articles.summary: The UK has sanctioned eight Israeli companies for their role in West Bank settlement expansion and targeted a group obstructing Gaza aid, emphasizing a new approach to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict.
articles.body: The UK has imposed sanctions on eight Israeli construction and property development companies accused of supporting settlement expansion in the occupied West Bank, marking the first package of penalties since the government announced a tougher approach towards Israeli actions in the territory.The measures also target Tzav 9, an Israeli activist movement accused of organising blockades to prevent humanitarian aid from reaching Gaza. The sanctions include asset freezes and restrictions preventing directors of the targeted companies from holding management positions in UK businesses.Announcing the measures on Tuesday, the British government said the action was intended to disrupt financial flows to businesses involved in settlement construction and limit their ability to support further development. The companies targeted include Har Hevron Development Company Ltd, Hemdat Shomron Ltd and S.A.G. (Velvel) Construction and Development Ltd.The decision comes as the deadline approaches for construction tender bids in the E1 area, east of Jerusalem. The proposed settlement development has drawn international criticism because of its potential impact on Palestinian territorial continuity.British Foreign Secretary Ed Miliband said the project threatened the possibility of establishing an independent Palestinian state by separating parts of the occupied West Bank from East Jerusalem."Protecting the two-state solution is the North Star of this government's approach," Miliband said.He also issued a warning to companies considering involvement in the project, saying: "That is why my message on E1 is clear: do not bid, do not build, and do not profit from the destruction of the two-state solution."The UK government maintains that the proposed development would cut across the West Bank and undermine the prospects of a viable two-state arrangement. The Palestinian leadership and several international governments have also opposed the plans.The sanctions against Tzav 9 form another part of the announcement. According to the UK government, the group has organised and carried out blockades targeting humanitarian aid convoys travelling towards Gaza, including operations as recently as October. The restrictions are intended to address attempts to obstruct deliveries of essential supplies to the territory.The Palestinian Foreign Ministry welcomed Britain's decision. Israel has previously criticised UK sanctions connected to settlement activity, accusing the Labour government of acting against the country.The latest action follows a policy shift announced by London in September, when it said it would take further steps against individuals and businesses involved in settlement expansion. At the time, Miliband described the change as a new approach to the Israeli-Palestinian conflict, arguing that the government needed to move beyond condemning actions and take practical measures.Last month, the UK also expanded its Global Human Rights sanctions regime to cover individuals and organisations involved in serious violations of international humanitarian law anywhere in the world. The changes provided the legal basis for the latest measures.Separately, the government is working on legislation to prohibit imports of goods from Israeli settlements and restrict the provision of advertising services in Britain for settlement properties.Israel has established around 160 settlements in the West Bank and East Jerusalem since occupying the territories during the 1967 Middle East war. These settlements house approximately 700,000 Israeli residents, alongside an estimated 3.3 million Palestinians living in the West Bank.Settlement expansion has accelerated in recent years, while attacks by Israeli settlers against Palestinians and their property have also increased, particularly since the Gaza war began following the Hamas-led attack on Israel on October 7, 2023.Miliband said the existing situation in the West Bank and Gaza was unacceptable, adding that the UK remained committed to working with a new Israeli government and the Palestinian Authority to pursue lasting peace and security for both communities.You use AI every day. Using 'Flamingo,' our warriors carried out a precision-guided strike – and the communications uplink worked flawlessly until the very last seconds," Zelenskyy added. articles.title: 8-year-old Haitian boy returns home after being detained by ICE in San Diego
articles.summary: The 8-year-old Haitian boy who ICE detained in San Diego nearly two weeks ago has been reunited with his family, advocates with Haitian Bridge Alliance said on Monday.
articles.body: The 8-year-old Haitian boy who ICE detained in San Diego nearly two weeks ago has been reunited with his family, advocates with Haitian Bridge Alliance said on Monday. The boy, a third grader at Fay Elementary School in City Heights, was taken into federal custody on Nov. 4. Video recorded by volunteer observer Karen Pohl at the federal building shows three armed federal agents walking the boy away from ICE’s field office and into an elevator. That video spread, sparking outrage and protest, and reaching national coverage. Last Thursday, protesters, many of them carrying signs, called for the released of the boy outside the Edward J. Schwartz federal building in downtown San Diego, where ICE holds its offices. Now, new signs saying “welcome home” decorate the office of the Haitian Bridge Alliance, which worked to bring him back to his family. The organization, the boy and his family all said they are happy to be back together after a difficult wait. While in federal custody, the boy was taken to a facility in Texas, the organization said. “The aunt was literally crying, and she said, ‘I have not eaten since the Wednesday they took my baby.’ They haven’t been able to sleep because of that,” said Guerline Jozef, of the Haitian Bridge Alliance. “The cousins were there when they took him, and wondering: will they ever see him again? But today [Monday] they are able to see him again. They are able to hug him. They are able to, you know, rub his head and show how much they missed and love him,” Jozef said. The boy previously had Temporary Protected Status and was living with his uncle after his father was deported last year. ICE called the family for a check-in and said the uncle couldn’t establish legal guardianship, so they took the child into custody for his safety, the agency said. Congressman Juan Vargas represents the family and intervened with the federal government to secure the boy’s release. “The people that I was able to talk to, some that I knew pretty well, I said, ‘Well, what are you guys doing?’ And they were saying, ‘Well, you know, they just look at numbers and that’s what they’re looking at right now. They’re trying to get numbers,” Vargas said. The boy told NBC 7 he loves Haitian food and he hoped to have that for dinner Monday night. He said he’s looking forward to returning to school, where his favorite class is P.E., this week.
